sources.title: Oda Nobunaga
sources.note: 1551 heads the clan, Owari; 1559 uncontested rule in Owari; June 1560 Imagawa Yoshimoto killed; 1567 Mino and Inabayama renamed Gifu; 1567-1568 Ise invasions; 9 Nov 1568 Kyoto, Rokkaku driven out of southern Omi; early 1570 Echizen; July 1570 Odani; Aug 1570 Ishiyama; 1573 end of Azai and Asakura; Azuchi 1576-1579; 1580 Ishiyama surrenders; 1581 Iga conquered; 1582 Nobutada and Ieyasu conquered Shinano and Kai; died 21 June 1582.

sources.title: Oda clan
sources.note: Home provinces Echizen and Owari; 1538 Nobuhide took Nagoya Castle; 1542 Nagoya to Nobunaga; 1555 Nobunaga killed his uncle at Kiyosu; Honno-ji 1582, the Oda briefly titular overlords of central Japan before Hideyoshi's family surpassed them; four Edo domains; 1871 kazoku.

sources.title: Honnō-ji Incident
sources.note: 21 June 1582, Akechi Mitsuhide with 13,000 soldiers at Honno-ji and Nijo Palace; central Japan firmly under Nobunaga after Tenmokuzan; Yamazaki two weeks later; Kiyosu Conference to determine the Oda successor.

sources.title: Azuchi–Momoyama period
sources.note: Nobunaga routed the Rokkaku in southern Omi, conquered Mino before 1568, tightened his grip on the Kinai after 1568; Ishiyama surrendered 1580 after an 11-year siege; Azuchi 1576-1579; after 1584 Hideyoshi ruler of the former Oda domains.

sources.title: Ishiyama Hongan-ji War
sources.note: August 1570 to August 1580, Ishiyama Hongan-ji in today's Osaka; Nagashima 1571 and 1574; Oda victory, the fortress burned.

sources.title: Sengoku period
sources.note: Okehazama 1560; Kyoto 1568, Matsunaga Hisahide relinquishes the city; Odani and Ichijodani 1573; Ishiyama 1580; Iga ikki destroyed 1581; Honno-ji 1582; Ieyasu gained much of Kai and Shinano in the Tensho-Jingo war.

sources.title: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
sources.note: 1573 Nobunaga appoints Hideyoshi daimyo of three districts in northern Omi; Chugoku campaign 1577-1582; Takamatsu June 1582 and peace with the Mori; Kiyosu conference chose Oda Hidenobu; Shizugatake 1583, some 30 provinces.

sources.title: Akechi Mitsuhide
sources.note: 1571 Sakamoto; 1575 sent to take Tanba; 1578 second siege of Kuroi, awarded Kameyama and Tanba Province, 550,000 koku; 1579 Tanba pacified; 21 June 1582 Honno-ji; 2 July 1582 Yamazaki.

sources.title: Takigawa Kazumasu
sources.note: 1567 and 1568 Ise invasions; Ise land about 1569; Nagashima lord 1574-1583; Kanto-kanrei with a portion of Kozuke after the 1582 Takeda campaign; lost at Kanagawa 1582 to the Hojo and went back to Ise.

sources.title: Siege of Miki
sources.note: Harima 1578-1580, Bessho Nagaharu against Hideyoshi for Nobunaga; Miki Castle fell to the Oda; the Akamatsu, Bessho and Kodera had submitted.

sources.title: Matsunaga Hisahide
sources.note: Daimyo of Yamato 1559 to 19 Nov 1577; 1568 submitted to Nobunaga and kept Yamato; died at Shigisan 1577; successor Tsutsui Junkei.

sources.title: Tenshō Iga War
sources.note: First war 6-7 Oct 1579 Iga victory; second war 30 Sept to 8 Oct 1581 Oda victory, Iga Province brought under Oda control.

sources.title: Uesugi Kagekatsu
sources.note: 1579 division lets Oda generals take Uesugi lands in Kaga, Noto and Etchu; 1582 Tenjinyama; Uozu fell 3 June 1582.

sources.title: Uesugi Kenshin
sources.note: 1577 Kenshin secured Noto and Kaga from the Oda clan.

sources.title: Takeda Katsuyori
sources.note: 2 March 1582 Takato lost; 11 March 1582 Tenmokuzan, end of the clan; used for the month only.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from fourteen pages (Oda Nobunaga, Oda clan, Honnō-ji Incident, Azuchi–Momoyama period, Ishiyama Hongan-ji War, Sengoku period, Toyotomi Hideyoshi, Akechi Mitsuhide, Takigawa Kazumasu, Siege of Miki, Matsunaga Hisahide, Tenshō Iga War, Uesugi Kagekatsu, Uesugi Kenshin, Takeda Katsuyori for the month). A Sengoku daimyo domain inside Cliopatria's single Warring States Japan row. Dated by the pages: Owari (1559), Mino (1567), Ise (1567-1568), Kyoto and southern Ōmi (Nov 1568), northern Ōmi and the Asakura end (1573), Tanba (1579), Harima (1580), Ishiyama (Aug 1580), Iga (Oct 1581), Kai and Shinano (1582). Not on the pages and so not drawn: Settsu, Kawachi, Izumi, Wakasa, Tango, Kii and Mikawa-side lands (the Azuchi–Momoyama page says only that he tightened his grip on 'the Kinai region' after 1568), the Echizen Ikkō-ikki, and the Nobunaga-era share of Shikoku or Chūgoku. The 1582 shape therefore under-draws central Japan; an area count is not claimed. Conflicts between pages: Nobunaga page has Nobutada and Ieyasu conquer Shinano and Kai in 1582; the Sengoku page gives Ieyasu 'much of Kai and Shinano' in the Tenshō-Jingo war; the Hideyoshi page gives 1577 and the Nobunaga page 1577 and 1578 for the Chūgoku dispatch; the Kenshin page says Kenshin took Noto and Kaga 'from the Oda' in 1577 while the Kagekatsu page has Oda generals take them in 1579 (this dossier carries only the 1579 gain, as no page dates an earlier Oda hold). The Oda lived on as four Edo domains (Tendō in Dewa 20,000 koku, Yanagimoto and Kaibara/Shibamura in Yamato 10,000 koku each, Kaibara in Tanba 20,000 koku; Oda clan page); not modelled here. End at Honnō-ji (21 June 1582) although the Oda clan page says they 'briefly remained titular overlords'. Counterpart strings: 'toyotomi-clan' (dossier to be written next), 'mori-clan' and 'imagawa-clan' (no dossier yet), 'takeda-clan' and 'uesugi-clan' (mirrors; both exist), plus persons and clans named in the pages. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
